questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Being able to participate in language-courses of higher level, due to pre-knowledge of the language. Getting to know the culture better, as a person living there. Overall just experiencing living abroad.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The host university was good at giving the needed information. I sometimes had issues with understanding the information and getting contact to administration from my home university though.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an arrival service in the beginning where I received all needed information. Thereto several introduction meetings online.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very complicated and hard. I was lucky to have personal contacts. Be in good time!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive and you should not expect to get housing on campus. Otherwise it gives good opportunities to know actual citizens, who are not students and see different parts of the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When showing up at the arrival service, I was handed the papers I needed to fill out with detailed descriptions and students from the university assisted with guidance. Thereto, I had a contact person from my department, who we could always contact.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Other students and administrative employees from the university. And during the courses you could always receive help from teachers.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was easy. I got the courses I wanted. But there was not that many to choose between.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the mails and don't be afraid to ask even the most simple questions, they are there to help you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses adapted with my level of skill. Maybe they were a little easier than what I am used to, but the courses did not match my field of interest completely, so it seemed to fit.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style was very similar, but the courses were shorter and therefore more intense. In general the teachers were good and had a very calm approach to studying, which I enjoyed.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Editing and Publishing in English Literature (7.5 ECTS) 
Film Experience: Theories and approaches (7.5 ECTS) 
Postmodern French Thinkers (7.5 ECTS) 
Mediatized Intersections: Class, Ethnicity, Gender, Sexuality (7.5 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: "Editing and Publishing in English Literature" and "Postmodern French Thinkers" were two very good courses, where I gained a lot of new knowledge. The teachers were very good.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping became more and more expensive during my stay due to the inflation.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were some social clubs and open bars on fridays, sportsclubs, language-courses

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend language courses, you meet a lot of different people from all over the world

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to museums, there are plenty of them, and are usually interesting in architecture, communication and knowledge.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, but probably because I stayed with Scandinavia.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is hard. Participating in group work after class and on-campus activities is a good start. Otherwise going to sports off campus helped me a lot.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The swedes tend to be a bit closed at first, but when you get to know them, they are very lovely people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There is a huge appreciation of coffee breaks and nature in Sweden, that I really enjoyed.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Everything is hard in the beginning, but you will find your way and the people you need. And just show up for things, participate. Maybe only once, but then you'll find out if it is you thing or not to do.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university is a bit small, use the city libraries to study.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living abroad, the experience itself of being away from home, knowing that I able to settle on my own.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding and the most challenging part for me was living abroad.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
